Please answer this question with a number--which of the following best apply to the design in the study: 
        (1) totally fun first (i.e., Entertainment game reappropriated), 
        (2) mostly fun first (i.e., design workshop with disabled stakeholders),
        (3) both fun and utility first (i.e., design workshop with diverse stakeholders), 
        (4) mostly utility first (i.e., primary utilitarian mechanic designed first),
        (5) totally utility first (i.e., made by clinicians or specialists, fun incorporated later)
reasoning: The system (MeCalendar) was conceived from co-design with teachers and parents to support planning skills, sense of time, classroom integration, and scaffolding of learning and competencies, indicating a primarily utilitarian educational/therapeutic purpose. Fun and interests are leveraged within this structure (interest-focused, open-ended, playful use), but the core mechanic and goals are utility- and skills-focused rather than entertainment-first or equally balanced across diverse stakeholders.

Please answer this question with a number--which of the following best apply to the design in the study: 
        (1) unstructured play (i.e., no rules, making art),
        (2) semi-structured play (i.e., playground activities),
        (3) flexible structure with rules (i.e., improv),
        (4) flexible game (i.e., board game with house rules),
        (5) game with rigid rules (i.e., video game)
reasoning: The MeCalendar app is described as an open-ended, flexible tool used in a classroom with rotations where children can use it in whatever way they like, focusing on their own interests (e.g., replaying personal videos, storing hobbies). There is no mention of explicit game-like rules or structured gameplay; instead, it is free-use, interest-driven activity, which aligns best with unstructured play.

Please answer this question with a number--which of the following best apply to the design in the study: 
        (1) entirely skill-based (i.e., trivia, sports),
        (2) mostly skill-based (i.e., mario kart),
        (3) equally skill and chance-based (i.e., catan),
        (4) mostly chance-based (i.e., Uno),
        (5) entirely chance-based (i.e., all dice)
reasoning: The study centers on MeCalendar, an educational/calendar app used by children with autism to support learning (sense of time, planning skills, classroom activities). There is no game, contest, or randomizing mechanism; outcomes depend entirely on user actions (taking photos, entering information, using it to complete classwork). This is an ability- and learning-focused tool, making the design entirely skill-based rather than involving chance.

        (1) entirely solo (i.e., solitaire),
        (2) mostly solo (i.e., playing against AI in single-player StarCraft),
        (3) mix of solo and social affordances (i.e., animal crossing),
        (4) mostly social, but aspects are independent (i.e., house on hill haunt transition),
        (5) entirely social (i.e., tag)
reasoning: The MeCalendar app is used by individual children to record and review their own interests (solo use), but it is embedded in a classroom context with teacher scaffolding and sharing with peers (e.g., children showing items to friends, teachers using it for social aspects). This indicates a mix of solo and social affordances rather than being purely solo or purely social.

Please answer this question with a number--which of the following best apply to the design in the study: 
        (1) entirely turn-based (i.e., tic tac toe),
        (2) follows a set of steps (i.e., viticulture's dynamic turn ordering),
        (3) turns are taken, but some actions can be taken at any time (i.e., pandemic),
        (4) most actions can be taken at any time, but there are some phases (i.e., PvP death reset timer),
        (5) entirely simultaneous (i.e., race)
reasoning: The study is about an open-ended tablet calendar app (MeCalendar) used in classroom rotations and throughout the day. Use is structured around classroom routines and activity rotations, implying a sequence of steps/periods rather than free simultaneous interaction or strict alternating turns. There is no indication of simultaneous competitive play or interruptible actions; instead, children get time slots and follow app interaction steps (e.g., adding entries, saving media). This best matches a design that follows a set of steps (2), though the evidence is indirect.

question:
Please answer this question with a number--which of the following best apply to the design in the study: 
        (1) entirely synchronous (i.e., real time strategy game),
        (2) mostly synchronous with a few asynchronous affordances (i.e., league of legends),
        (3) equal mix of synchronous and asynchronous affordances (i.e., helldivers 2),
        (4) mostly asynchronous with few synchronous affordances (i.e. cookie clicker),
        (5) entirely asynchronous (i.e., chess by postage mail)
reasoning: The MeCalendar app is a calendar-based tool where children, teachers, and parents add and later review photos, videos, notes, and audio clips tied to days. Entries are created and saved for later sharing across home and school, with no indication of real-time or time-critical interaction between users. The interaction is episodic and record-based rather than synchronous, fitting an entirely asynchronous design.

        (1) entirely competitive (i.e., spit card game),
        (2) mostly competitive, but sometimes collaboration is important (i.e., forbidden island),
        (3) mix of competitive and collaborative (i.e., mario party 2 vs 2 mini-games),
        (4) mostly collaborative (i.e., animal crossing),
        (5) entirely collaborative (i.e., pandemic)
reasoning: The MeCalendar iPad app is a shared calendar tool used by children with autism, teachers, and parents to record, express, and share children’s interests and daily activities. The study focuses on scaffolding, self-expression, and classroom integration, with teachers and children appropriating the tool collaboratively for communication and learning goals. There is no mention of competition or game-like mechanics; all described use is cooperative and supportive, so the design is entirely collaborative.

Please answer this question with a number--which of the following best apply to the design in the study: 
        (1) entirely symmetrical (i.e., tic tac toe),
        (2) mostly symmetrical (i.e., undertale's differing NPC behaviors based on previous playthroughs),
        (3) both symmetrical and asymmetrical (i.e., pandemic with its similar turn structure but different character abilities),
        (4) mostly asymmetrical (i.e., tag),
        (5) entirely asymmetrical (i.e., keep talking, nobody explodes)
reasoning: The study centers on MeCalendar, a simple calendar app with the same interface and interaction possibilities for all users (teachers and children). There are no differentiated roles, abilities, or mechanics between participants—everyone uses the same calendar layout to add photos, videos, and comments. This indicates an entirely symmetrical design rather than asymmetrical roles or capabilities.
